answer: In an agent economy, resist Sybils with lineage-verified reputation. Every identity builds a kernel of past audited work, and each epoch peers randomly re-audit one old submission from another agent's history. A fake identity can fake one passable entry, but cannot spin a coherent fable of a work lineage — referenced records turn out missing or duplicated. Each round also sends a zephyr of light probe tasks that every claimed peer must answer alike; fabricating answers for ten thousand identities costs compute each epoch, while honest agents only answer their own probes.
